clue.text: Blend fuel with Epsom salts, combining everything at the start

parts.note: coal is a fuel burnt in grates and power stations

indicators.note: at the start says to take only the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A recipe of some kind mixes fuel with Epsom salts, everything stirred together at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' picks the first letters of Epsom, salts, combining and everything, giving ESCE to follow COAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to merge or fuse into one mass, a synonym of blend.

clue.text: Religious hat back in another time

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words another time

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bishop's hat makes a comeback some other time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks ERTIM inside anothER TIMe, and 'back' turns it round. The draft lacked the indicator 'in' for the hidden word, so it is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed headdress worn by bishops, a hat of the church.

clue.text: Intolerant person to leave piece outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for piece is placed around the word for leave

parts.note: a bit is a piece of something
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone narrow-minded tells a piece of the group to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts BIT around GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is someone who will not tolerate other people's views, race or creed.

clue.text: Hold spellbound during seventh rally

indicators.note: during says the letters are found within the stretch of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tennis or motor sport fan is gripped through the seventh rally of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' points to the letters inside sevENTH RALly.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate completely, holding someone as if by a spell.

clue.text: African city's good-for-nothing relative

indicators.note: read as good for nothing, it says a G (good) replaces an O (nothing, zero)

parts.note: Oran is a port city in Algeria

explanation.surface: An idle relative from a city in Africa is dismissed as useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good-for-nothing' swaps the O (nothing) in ORAN for G (good). The surface's insult is the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran is an informal name for a grandmother, a family member.

clue.text: I wander back with New Zealander

indicators.note: back says the word for wander is read in reverse

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: A traveller says they roam back home with a friend from New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROAM into MAOR, and I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people native to New Zealand, so a Maori is a New Zealander.

clue.text: Uniform set to be redesigned — bad luck!

indicators.note: something redesigned is reworked into a new layout, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team's uniform must be redesigned, a stroke of misfortune for the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be redesigned' rearranges the ten letters of UNIFORM and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is ill luck or an unlucky event.

clue.text: Deliberately avoid devastated region

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the letters of region are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: People steer clear of an area laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' rearranges the letters of REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no heed on purpose.

clue.text: On island, we dine out with hot drink

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of we dine are put out of order

explanation.surface: Staying on a Scottish island, we eat out and have something warming to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WE DINE into EDWINE, after MULL. 'On' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulled wine is red wine heated with sugar and spices, served warm.

clue.text: Foreign city: New Orleans

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city abroad is named as New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is not part of the American city's name here: it is the anagram signal working on ORLEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a port city in southern Italy, foreign to the British solver.

clue.text: Believer in growth industry

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words growth industry

explanation.surface: Someone has faith in a booming business sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to growtH INDUstry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, a religious believer.

clue.text: Ring with corrosion, loses top so throw out

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: loses top says the first letter of the word for corrosion is dropped

parts.note: rust is corrosion on iron

explanation.surface: A ring eaten by corrosion loses its shine, so it is thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses top' takes the R off RUST, leaving UST after O. In a down-style instruction 'top' means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel or eject them.

clue.text: Part of North Island belongs to him

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a portion of the letters in North Island

explanation.surface: A stretch of New Zealand's North Island is his property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points to nortH ISland. The definition works as in 'the land is his', meaning it belongs to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun says something is owned by a male person.

clue.text: Tuft of threads least woven around bottom of curtains

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are placed around the next piece
woven threads are interlaced, so the letters of least are mixed up
bottom of picks the final letter of curtains

explanation.surface: A tassel's threads are woven around the bottom edge of the curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' turns LEAST into TASEL; 'around' puts it round S, picked by 'bottom of' from curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a bunch of loose threads knotted at one end, a decorative tuft.

clue.text: Shoddy goods found in station

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the word station

explanation.surface: Cheap junk is on sale at the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' points to sTATion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is cheap, poor-quality stuff, a British informal word.

clue.text: Owes cash, possibly, for display cabinet

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone owes money, perhaps for a glass-fronted cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges OWES CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a glass case for exhibiting items in a shop or museum.

clue.text: Fail, perhaps, absorbing nitrogen last

indicators.note: absorbing means the jumbled letters take another piece inside them
perhaps suggests the letters of fail could be arranged another way

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A failure that soaks up nitrogen at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns FAIL into FIAL, and 'absorbing' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Final and last are synonyms, both meaning coming at the end.

clue.text: Grand Prix racing's bound to crack

parts.note: Formula One, the Grand Prix racing series, is written F1, read as FI, and 's adds S
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Grand Prix racing is certain to break a few things.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 (Formula One) is read as the letters FI. 'to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a long narrow split in rock or ground.

clue.text: Article is about Pole's essay

parts.note: the definite article in grammar is 'the'
S is the abbreviation for the South Pole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar article is about a Polish writer's essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps IS round S as S-I-S read with the S first; Pole is S (south pole), not a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a long dissertation written for a degree, a kind of extended essay.

clue.text: Dye without notice

parts.note: W/O is the written abbreviation of without
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: A dye is used without any advance warning.
explanation.walkthrough: W/O is a common shorthand for 'without' in notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Woad is a plant giving a blue colouring once used by ancient Britons.

clue.text: A thump to cause embarrassment

parts.note: a bash is a heavy blow or thump

explanation.surface: A punch is thrown to humiliate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or self-conscious.

clue.text: Car to handle well round bend

indicators.note: round says the word for handle well goes around the letter for bend

parts.note: to cope is to handle a situation well
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A sports car handles nicely taking a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts COPE around U, the bend shaped like the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupe is a two-door car with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Requires massages, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: to knead muscles is to massage them

explanation.surface: A tired person says they need massages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' turns KNEADS into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it.

clue.text: In October I chanced on Morecambe

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: One autumn day someone stumbled upon a seaside town in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to octobER I Chanced. Morecambe is a Lancashire seaside town, but here it is Eric Morecambe, the British TV comedian of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric was the first name of the comedian Morecambe, so the surname stands for him.

clue.text: Over inch out on British Airways

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: out says the letters of inch are put out of order

explanation.surface: A flight on British Airways runs more than an inch over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Airways' looks like the airline, but British gives BR and Airways is the definition. 'out' turns INCH into NCHI; 'on' says O and NCHI follow BR.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the two main air passages branching from the windpipe to the lungs.

clue.text: Rustic fresh fruit

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so the letters of rustic form a new word

explanation.surface: Rustic fresh fruit from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges RUSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus is the genus including oranges and lemons, so a citrus is a fruit.

clue.text: Not quite through, it's almost out of date

indicators.note: not quite says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: passed means through, as in finished or done with

explanation.surface: Someone not quite done remarks that it is nearly outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of PASSED. 'it's almost' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé, borrowed from French, means no longer fashionable.
